x: We were also pleased to see Harry Greene turning out over the country and there were also several other new faces on view. The placings resulted as follows: 1, Maclean; 2, Stearman; 3, Adams, 4, Greene; 5, Simpson; 6, Butt; 7, Udall; 8, Courtney; 9, Cornell; 10, Corpe; 11, Tomlinson; 12, Harvey.

Godfrey, but Harry Greene had bad luck seeing that at one time he was in the lead with Maclean but they went off the course, and although Maclean managed to regain the lead Greene found the effort too much for him and finished further back.
Placings of our club members were as under:—Maclean, 1; Adams, P., 2; Wolton, 3; Simpson, 5; Greene, 6; Courtney, 7; Grieves, 8; Butt, 9; Udall, 11.

The 1 mile (under 19) event saw the limit man retain his lead throughout, with Harry Greene making a good effort to overtake him. Peter Courtney was third and Don Maclean, who was the scratch man, seemed to be having a training run only.

Our team was minus Len Herbert and Len Adams, not to mention Jack Braughton and Jimmy Wood, who are eligible for this event, so that although we were pressed rather closely by Herne Hill Harriers, who had Greene, of Reading, assisting them, we can be quite satisfied with the actual result.
Fast times had already been thrown up as Boldon and Greene had gone to 9.87 and 9.90 in heat 1 but the Belgravian raised his game again and this time broke new ground with a 10.13.
